draft: I am writing to formally report the theft of my mobile phone, which occurred on [DATE AND TIME OF INCIDENT] at Lajpat Nagar market. When I approached [POLICE STATION] to report this incident, the officers on duty refused to register an FIR and instead advised me to file an online lost report. I am deeply concerned by this refusal. My device contains active banking applications and UPI credentials, making me highly vulnerable to potential financial fraud. I request you to clarify the legal basis for refusing to register an FIR in this case, as I understand that the police are mandated to register an FIR for cognizable offences. Please register an FIR immediately regarding this theft, provide me with a free copy of the registered FIR, and initiate an investigation to recover the device. Given the presence of sensitive financial data on the phone, I urge you to treat this matter with the necessary urgency to prevent any unauthorized transactions.

# Formal Complaint: Request for Registration of FIR regarding theft of mobile phone

**To:** The Station House Officer, [POLICE STATION] Police Station (submit at the police station or on your state police portal)

Aapka phone Lajpat Nagar market mein chori hua hai aur police ne FIR likhne se mana kar diya hai. Is letter mein humne SHO se FIR register karne aur investigation shuru karne ki maang ki hai. Saath hi, humne ye bhi pucha hai ki kya police FIR likhne se mana kar sakti hai, kyunki phone mein banking apps aur UPI hain.

```
To,
The Station House Officer
[POLICE STATION] Police Station


Date: 09 October 2026

Subject: Formal Complaint: Request for Registration of FIR regarding theft of mobile phone

Dear Sir/Madam,

I am writing to formally report the theft of my mobile phone, which occurred on [DATE AND TIME OF INCIDENT] at Lajpat Nagar market. When I approached [POLICE STATION] to report this incident, the officers on duty refused to register an FIR and instead advised me to file an online lost report. I am deeply concerned by this refusal. My device contains active banking applications and UPI credentials, making me highly vulnerable to potential financial fraud. I request you to clarify the legal basis for refusing to register an FIR in this case, as I understand that the police are mandated to register an FIR for cognizable offences. Please register an FIR immediately regarding this theft, provide me with a free copy of the registered FIR, and initiate an investigation to recover the device. Given the presence of sensitive financial data on the phone, I urge you to treat this matter with the necessary urgency to prevent any unauthorized transactions.

Yours faithfully,
[YOUR NAME]
[PHONE]
[EMAIL]
[ADDRESS]

Keep a copy and ask for a signed, stamped receipt (or the FIR copy) when you submit this.
```

## Where to report, and if the police don't act
1. **National Cyber Crime Helpline 1930 / cybercrime.gov.in** (call 1930 · report on cybercrime.gov.in · call your bank to block the account/card) — Immediately — within hours if possible, so the money can be traced and frozen. Note the acknowledgement number and quote it in your police complaint. https://cybercrime.gov.in · 1930
2. **Station House Officer (SHO), [POLICE STATION]** (written complaint at the police station · e-FIR on your state police citizen portal where available) — Give your written complaint at the police station. For a cognizable offence the police must register an FIR; you can report at any police station (zero FIR) and you are entitled to a free copy. Get a signed and stamped receipt for your written complaint. · 112
3. **Superintendent of Police / Deputy Commissioner of Police** (complaint in writing by registered post or in person) — If the SHO refuses to register an FIR: send the substance of your complaint in writing to the SP/DCP (BNSS, 2023, s.173(4)). Keep the postal receipt.
4. **Judicial Magistrate** (application through a lawyer or the District Legal Services Authority (free if eligible)) — If the police still do not act: apply to the Magistrate to direct registration and investigation (BNSS, 2023, s.175(3)). https://nalsa.gov.in · 15100

_Information, not legal advice._
